title: Audio concurrency scaling: mixed prefill, state ownership and codec overlap
summary: Diagnose audio scaling with scheduler-step counts, admission/drain phases, mixed prefill/decode and codec overlap; isolate state, label and RNG ownership before qualifying same-source service throughput and complete audio quality.

zh-CN.title: 音频并发扩展：混合预填充、状态归属和 codec 重叠
zh-CN.summary: 按调度轮而非图碎片计数，分开初始填充、持续接纳与排空阶段，分析混合预填充/解码和 codec 重叠；分别检查状态、标签及随机数归属，再以同源服务对照和完整音频质量验收。

hardware: CUDA GPUs supported by the pinned runtime and operators; qualify the actual SKU separately
conditions: The model uses autoregressive acoustic frames, a codebook tower, recurrent GDN state and a streaming codec.
Resolve effective stage settings, CUDA graph buckets, precision and dependencies from the selected revision; deployment comments are not local benchmark evidence.

recommendations: Measure low and high concurrency independently. Attribute pure decode, prompt work, admission gaps and codec work using actual active batch sizes, not the configured capacity alone.

Count scheduler steps from the owning CPU execution annotation or scheduler metadata. A PIECEWISE step can launch many graph fragments; grouping kernel names or graph launches is not a step count. Correlate optional GPU spans explicitly and preserve their scope.

Separate initial fill, ongoing request admission and final drain before interpreting batch occupancy. Retain whole-run statistics and phase definitions; client in-flight counts include queueing and codec work and are not direct active-model counts or proof of a steady state.

A mixed backbone can share projection and MoE execution across prompt and decode rows while keeping causal attention and recurrent updates segmented. Measure whether joint rows amortize work on the real workload; preserving the expert count alone does not preserve backend dispatch or rounding.

The source deployment combines chunked prefill, asynchronous CPU scheduling, FULL decode graphs, PIECEWISE mixed graphs, and a stateful codec on overlapping CUDA execution. Test these mechanisms individually when porting the design.

Preserve decode-first ordering and per-request state indices in a mixed step. Each convolution and recurrent state must advance exactly once; fresh state rows must be reset without affecting other requests.
Keep acoustic prompt rows in cache identity: the source disables prefix caching because token-ID hashing does not cover their code values.

Retain the codec chunk ramp, left context, complete emitted audio and preparation costs while comparing schedules. Do not substitute a kernel timing or text-token rate for playable-audio service throughput.

Use hardware counters on actual routed inputs to distinguish tensor arithmetic from expert-weight traffic. Report profiler replay policy, measured DRAM bytes and peak fraction, layer/input coverage and routing-count provenance; low tensor activity is not a directly recoverable speedup.

Inspect static maximum sequence lengths separately from real packed token counts. Tighter graph bounds can remove inactive recurrent chunks and attention work without changing rows; validate every real and padding sequence fits, preserve a larger-bound fallback, and compare all state and outputs before service.

For stochastic service A/B trials, retain generated-frame counts and request-length differences alongside frames/s and drain duration. Capture warmups and scheduling can change random draws, so a faster makespan alone does not prove a fixed-work kernel gain.

Separate replay streams and graph memory pools do not by themselves prove BLAS scratch isolation. Inspect the installed runtime capture/workspace ownership; where buffers are keyed by capture stream, test dedicated capture streams and record actual address ranges. Compare identical dynamic admissions, RNG, slot reuse and full mutable state before attributing a failure to workspace sharing.

An achieved isolated full-batch decode rate is a workload-specific reference, not a hardware upper bound or a service lower bound. Account for real prompt work, partial batches, codec interference and complete drain before judging the service target.

For asynchronous timelines, compute model/codec interval unions and their intersection before attributing elapsed time. Record actual decode steps, active rows, mixed token capacity and exact codec grouping rather than inferring GPU work from client concurrency.

Distinguish codec frame-bucket diversity from same-bucket partitioning. Log each ready group, chosen partition, actual request count and actual captured graph size; a planned oversized batch can be rounded differently by the graph dispatcher.

Compact packed recurrent chunk descriptors once per replay, preserve the original per-sequence recurrence ordering and arithmetic, and guard kernels that otherwise execute matrix work on invalid chunks. Recheck empty sequences, dynamic descriptor updates and larger-span fallback.

Reserved decode padding can use a shorter runtime attention context while preserving the largest capture plan, provided the graph explicitly identifies its private slots. Verify real outputs and all nonparticipating slots; do not infer a reserved range for arbitrary request-state callers.

Test stream contention on identical inputs and full restored state, comparing model-only, codec-only, serial and concurrent pair completion. A higher launch-stream priority is only a scheduling hint; query graph instantiation flags before interpreting priority trials.

For cross-stream model pipelines, establish both execution dependencies and allocation lifetimes. Retain a producer tensor until every consumer stream has finished; an event wait alone does not stop the allocator from reusing callback-local storage.

Derive inter-frame dependencies from the actual embedding and sampled-code paths before declaring a whole tower serial. Keep next-frame positions, attention workspaces, recurrent states and sampling counters independent until their required joins.

When changing codec resource allocation, verify actual captured kernel assignments and preserve the normal partition policy. If its measured cost table changes partitions, report that feedback explicitly rather than claiming a fixed-partition comparison.

Estimate temporal batching eligibility from observed chunk phases, admission and completion boundaries. Requests can have correlated emission phases; an independent per-row probability model can badly misestimate useful coverage.

Separate queued work from runnable admission when deciding whether to launch a bounded multi-step graph. Reuse the actual capacity, minimum-batch, minimum-running and oldest-age predicate; preserve pending-arrival and audio/completion boundaries. Record mutually exclusive decisions separately from overlapping context counters, and measure any extra admission delay.

Inspect compiled codec graphs for repeated casts of immutable Linear weights. Caching the existing autocast result can remove traffic without changing GEMM precision, but retain original reference/encoding modules and native norm/layer-scale precision. A compiler option alone is not proof that casts disappeared; inspect dispatched kernels and validate full codec state.

Inspect production-specialization register/shared-memory allocation when fusing recurrent operations. A debug output can change allocation, and removing launches can lose throughput through reduced residency or added synchronization; compile and measure the actual deployed specialization.

Control native algorithm-plan caches when comparing autotuning modes. Verify the installed cache key and lookup order: a flag change after control warmup may reuse the same plan. Isolate per-thread caches using fresh host threads where the implementation supports that scope, retain compilation/preparation costs, and do not clear shared system caches.

Use final SASS and actual launch resource attributes to audit register and shared-memory use. Source or intermediate-code register hints may not reach machine code; their sum cannot establish resident-block counts or an occupancy improvement.

Treat native routing metadata as a per-call ownership map: physical rows can be permuted legally. Validate bounds, token/expert bijection and valid-row prefixes using each implementation's own current map before comparing logical values; never infer a permutation from output values.

Compare complete calls at the same input/output boundary while retaining the baseline's production features, including programmatic dependent launch (PDL). Record candidate limitations explicitly; exact components, fewer global buffers or a faster fused kernel do not establish complete-call or service gains.

Moving a dependency wait requires proof that every earlier metadata read is ready. Record all metadata producers from actual capture provenance, add full-memory dependencies only where required, preserve consumer-side programmatic dependencies, and instantiate only after validating the complete graph and retained storage.

Audit the actual loaded shared-library path, version and binary identity before interpreting capability queries or cross-language comparisons. Loader search paths can override intended build linkage; preserve the original mismatch and keep unresolved precision capabilities unqualified even when finite fixtures match.

Record candidate eligibility and the number of calls actually replaced. If filtering selects no candidate or no replacement is chosen, the final comparison may execute the same implementation in both arms; its timing difference is control variation, not an optimization gain.

Separate measured resident CTAs and active warps from eligible warps and instruction issue. Increased occupancy without more issuable work does not establish more useful latency hiding; inspect weight traffic and dependency evidence before attributing a speedup.

Interpret stall-counter normalization explicitly. An aggregate long-scoreboard ratio per issue-active cycle is neither a wall-time fraction nor proof that TMA is the cause. Instruction attribution needs report-owned loaded-function identity and exact PC mapping; retain missing or out-of-function samples and unresolved replay-pass metadata.

Separate causal-prefix identity, compact operator parity and full graph timing. Identity must include acoustic code columns, conditioning, exact position and initial state; retain decode and private padding rows, preserve current routing ownership and count gather/expand and retained-buffer costs.

Before judging a candidate against an opaque native operator, validate the native control against an independently archived output and inspect the exact installed ABI. A wrong routing-scale flag can invalidate the control before any candidate comparison.

Build fusion budgets from the elapsed dependency path and required operations, not kernel counts or summed overlapping durations. Account for direct matrix operations outside intercepted helper calls, and distinguish arithmetic that remains required from removable boundaries.

Before discarding a reuse strategy, account for its adapters. A consumer can sometimes use an inverse ownership map directly instead of materializing expanded components; preserve the original residual rows, arithmetic and rounding, and include all gathers and copies in the same graph boundary.
Keep offline compilation and actual JIT binary identities separate. Resource counts and spill claims must refer to the deployed specialization, with the real strides, flags and launch configuration.

For transparent compressed allocations, query hardware support and verify each actual allocation property. Retain original tensor bytes, layout, scales, native kernels and captured owners; test both consumed and unconsumed ownership paths before native use. CPU entropy, requested flags and virtual capacity do not establish GPU compression ratio or speed.

Bound graph specialization by activation coverage and total readiness/memory cost. Keep unsupported shapes on the original graph, include CPU mapping and transfer costs in service timing, and validate shared graph-pool lifetimes separately from artifact-private buffers.

When a graph-shape comparison fails in private state, compare full physical input histories, including padding left by earlier replays. Preserve the failure, verify an unchanged A/A control and align inputs without filtering state or relaxing arithmetic gates.
validation_plan: L0: exercise partial batches, variable prompt boundaries, slot reuse, request cancellation and untouched-state checks before any service comparison.

For mixed execution, check state slots, teacher-forced labels and sampling/RNG ownership separately. Compare each changed layer on identical inputs, snapshot untouched slots before replay, exercise prompt boundaries and slot reuse, and preserve sampling-row and counter ordering in deterministic controls.

Record the model batch, prompt token budget and admission phase for every diagnosed scheduler step. Use a continuously replenished workload when investigating sustained scheduling; distinguish scheduled prompt chunks from unique requests and retain the final drain rather than silently filtering it.

When batched and single-request outputs differ, preserve the failed comparison and run the unchanged implementation through the same check. Isolate each changed operator on identical layer inputs to separate new errors from accumulated floating-point and routing differences; never silently relax its numeric threshold.

For stream overlap, hold request ordering, initial model/codec state and sampling counters fixed; compare generated codes, PCM, completion order and reused-slot state. Exact fixed-request replay does not replace quality under dynamic service admission.
L1/L2: replay heterogeneous real prompts; inspect routing occupancy and graph kernels, and distinguish summed kernel time from elapsed time when streams overlap.

L3/L4: score every output in the frozen corpus and repeated concurrency sweep; report acoustic frames/s, first playable audio latency, RTF, errors, WER and speaker similarity. Preserve rejected runs and source/environment provenance.

Promote a scheduling or kernel change only after a same-source end-to-end control/candidate comparison and complete repeated quality coverage meet the frozen gates. Operator checks, graph replay and a phase-selected trace cannot substitute for the full service result.

Preserve an original bit-exact failure when investigating a changed batch shape or numerical backend. Identify real versus private scratch slots, quantify PCM and state errors, and use an independent higher-precision reference or causal isolation. A later diagnostic does not rewrite the failed gate and does not replace full WER/SIM.

When an isolated kernel improvement fails the full service throughput score, retain frame-count, length and drain differences and the failed score. Use fixed-input timing to test the operator hypothesis; do not rescue acceptance by discarding tails or substituting a selected-phase rate.

A capture-versus-eager validator must retain references to the captured buffers: replay updates captured storage, while eager Python execution can rebind object attributes. Preserve any failing run and prove a validator-handle mistake before replacing its result.

Check compiler FMA contraction and intermediate rounding when fusing native arithmetic. A source-level cast sequence need not imply separate machine operations. Keep original failures and distinguish an explicit correction from a separately declared higher-precision numerical diagnostic.

Expand numerical checks across independently prepared real fixtures, layers and partial batches before timing. A single fixture can pass while another exposes small-magnitude per-head errors or a worse independent-reference error; retain both outcomes and preserve the predeclared gate.

For empty-work graph checks, retain mutable device sources and capture their metadata copies so the same executable can transition from empty to positive work and back. Check full dependency coverage, output guards, read-only inputs, RNG and restored state; do not silently include operations without a defined empty-work contract.

For compact prefix execution, reconstruct real full-row inputs and verify their hashes; compare native quantization, scales, routing and all output components before checking complete model state, unchanged slots, teacher outputs and RNG in one reused mixed graph.

For fixed-work graph timing, restore the same complete initial state before every measured replay in both arms. Record whether restore, host preparation and postgraph work are inside the timed boundary; repeated in-place state advancement is a different workload.

For an ownership map, reject stale same-length conditioning, preserve all acoustic columns and original padding/decode owners, and test changed slots and no-reuse fallback. Artifact-private storage does not qualify production graph-pool lifetimes.

Preserve an initial continuation failure when testing a separately frozen adapter. Distinguish same-capture timing rounds from independent process repetitions, and retain every pair plus complete restored-state checks.

After qualifying compact/reused graphs, measure complete service with actual activation counts, CPU preparation, memory/readiness, all output quality and full drain. A local repeated gain cannot override a failed predeclared service continuation gate.
limitations: This record describes source-grounded mechanisms, not a reproduced speedup or a portable set of tuned constants.
A low-concurrency improvement does not imply high-concurrency improvement; reducing admission wait can also increase costly mixed steps.
Changing state precision, codec precision or FP8 execution can affect generated samples. Operator parity alone does not establish end-to-end audio quality.
A faster isolated operation can still regress service throughput. Recheck the unchanged serving configuration and complete audio quality before choosing a fused kernel or a different batch policy.
CUDA event spans can include host-submission gaps. Do not label their union as SM utilization, or count overlapped codec duration again as an available end-to-end speedup.
Qualification of another engine or a different GPU requires its own acceptance issue and complete evidence.

A whole-run average batch can be dominated by drain steps; a high batch in an admission subset does not establish an end-to-end speedup. Phase cuts are diagnostic scope, not permission to remove requests from acceptance metrics.

A shared-execution prototype may change GEMM shapes, MoE implementation or random-number consumption. Keep those changes explicit, and keep timing from a device with observed external work unqualified even when numerical checks pass.

A kernel reading nearly one active-expert weight footprint can remain bandwidth-limited despite low tensor activity; row padding or inactive experts must not be converted directly into a speedup claim.

A dedicated capture stream is a workspace-isolation hypothesis, not proof that prior quality failures were races. Require a fixed dynamic schedule and full service quality before attributing a cause or selecting overlap.
Configured or logged SM reservations may apply to a routing subkernel rather than expert GEMMs; inspect the actual dispatched branch before using such a setting as a resource-allocation explanation.

Native codec re-batching can change floating-point rounding. An error confined to a private scratch slot differs from a live-state error, but neither scratch analysis nor a high PCM SNR establishes full service quality.

A selected-phase delivery rate can explain a changing service score but is not GPU effective batch or a replacement acceptance metric. High client occupancy only rules out client starvation within its measured scope.
